ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.claim: The passage exposes the baselessness of Quraysh's idols and intercessors, which they viewed as sources of success and feared abandoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.anchor: that if they left them, they would be destroyed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r4.claim: The second command to invoke partners follows their failed reply and mocks them, since their partners cannot help and they remain foolish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r4.anchor: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم: لما سئلوا أين شركاؤكم وأجابوا بغير جواب، سئلوا ثانيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r5.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil say the subject of ورأوا includes worshippers and worshipped; the conditional answer is generally inferred from context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل: هو للتابع والمتبوع، وجواب لو محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r6.claim: Al-Razi argues no answer is omitted: the call terrifies worshippers so they cannot see, or idols cannot see because they are not living.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وعندي أن الجواب غير محذوف، وفي تقريره وجوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r7.claim: The author rejects al-Razi's view because ورأوا most naturally refers to worshippers, and taking المهتدين to mean living beings is remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p318/r7.anchor: والظاهر أنه عائد على الداعين، كقوله: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r4.claim: The coming passage refutes polytheism and the belief that alleged partners or intercessors could benefit their worshippers in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p559/r4.anchor: a refutation of polytheism and idols

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r1.claim: After leaders disown the followers, the followers call on Arab deities such as Lāt, Manāt, ʿUzzā, and Nāʾilah, but receive no answer because these imagined deities never existed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r2.claim: The author distinguishes Arabia's imagined idols from worship of actual beings, which the Qur'an treats separately.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r2.anchor: are mentioned separately by the Qur’ ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r3.speaker: Jesus (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r3.claim: Jesus disowns those who worship him, says he did not know they did so, and says he had called people to worship the One God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r3.anchor: Jesus (sws) will disown those who worshipped him and say that he was

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r4.claim: Calling on idols in which the polytheists placed hope will be futile, while God's torment will confront them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r4.anchor: pinned their hopes will prove futile. However, the torment of God will be before them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r5.claim: The wish that the idolaters had been guided expresses sorrow over their state and shows how profound and terrible the torment is.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p563/r5.anchor: the torment becomes evident from this.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p7#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p7#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p7#2/r11.claim: The command to call the partners is chiefly a reproach, since the unbelievers know the partners cannot help; their failure to answer leaves punishment certain and warns people in this life.
RAZI-FULL:v25p7#2/r11.anchor: لأنهم يعلمون أنه لا فائدة في دعائهم لهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r1.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil take the omitted consequence to mean that the followers and followed see the punishment; had they been guided in worldly life, they would not see it in the Hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل يعني المتبوع والتابع يرون العذاب ولو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا ما أبصروه في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r2.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r2.claim: A second proposed completion is that, had they been guided in worldly life, they would have known the punishment was true.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r2.anchor: لو أنهم كانوا مهتدين في الدنيا لعلموا أن العذاب حق

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r3.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r3.claim: A third proposed completion is that when they see the punishment they will wish they had been guided in worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r3.anchor: ودوا حين رأوا العذاب لو كانوا في الدنيا يهتدون

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r4.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r4.claim: A fourth proposed completion is that they would have warded off the punishment if they had known any stratagem for doing so.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r4.anchor: لو كانوا يهتدون لوجه من وجوه الحيل لدفعوا به العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r5.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r5.claim: A fifth completion says it is now time for them to be guided when they see the punishment, supported by the verse that they will not believe until they see painful punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r5.anchor: قد آن لهم أن يهتدوا لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون إذا رأوا العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r6.claim: Al-Razi argues that the consequence of “if only they were guided” is not omitted; one reading is that the command to call their partners fills them with terror and dizziness, blinding them so they cannot see the punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r6.anchor: فههنا يشتد الخوف عليهم ويلحقهم شيء كالسدر والدوار

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r7.claim: A second reading takes the pronoun in “they saw” to refer to the idols: they would see the punishment if they were living and guided, but are not; the pronoun is acceptable because the preceding wording reflects the unbelievers' belief.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r7.anchor: أي هذه الأصنام كانوا يشاهدون العذاب لو كانوا من الأحياء المهتدين

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r8.claim: A third reading makes “seeing” inward: the unbelievers knew in worldly life that the punishment was true, had they been guided.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r8.anchor: أن يكون المراد من الرؤية رؤية القلب أي والكفار علموا حقية هذا العذاب في الدنيا لو كانوا يهتدون

RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r9.claim: Al-Razi considers these direct readings better than supplying an omitted consequence, which would break the verse's arrangement.
RAZI-FULL:v25p8/r9.anchor: وهذه الوجوه عندي خير من الوجوه المبنية على أن جواب لو محذوف فإن ذلك يقتضي تفكيك النظم من الآية

BURSEVI:v6p306/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p306/r6.claim: The keepers of Hell call on those who worshipped other than God to summon their idols and similar alleged partners, as a threat and rebuke.
BURSEVI:v6p306/r6.anchor: لمن عبد غير الله توبيخا وتهديدا والقائلون الخزنة

BURSEVI:v6p306/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p306/r7.claim: The idols are called their partners because the worshippers claimed that they were God's partners.
BURSEVI:v6p306/r7.anchor: أي : الأصنام ونحوها ليخلصوكم من العذاب أضافها إليهم

BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r1.claim: They summon the alleged partners out of extreme bewilderment.

BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r2.claim: The partners cannot answer or help because they have no power to respond or rescue them.
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r2.anchor: ضرورة عدم قدرتهم على الاستجابة والنصرة

BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r4.claim: If they had found a way to avert punishment or followed the truth in worldly life, they would not have suffered this torment.
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r4.anchor: لوجه من وجوه الحيل يدفعون به العذاب أو إلى الحق في الدنيا لما لقوا ما لقوا

BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r5.claim: Some read the conditional as a wish: they will wish they had been guided rather than astray.
BURSEVI:v6p306#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو للتمني هنا أي تمنوا لو أنهم كانوا مهتدين

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r1.claim: The partners are the objects idolaters worshipped instead of or alongside God; the commentary cites other verses about them.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r1.anchor: The idolaters are to call upon those whom they worshipped instead of or alongside God (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r2.claim: Some say the former idolaters will not even expect an answer from their former objects of worship, and that this is itself part of their chastisement.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r2.anchor: some commentators interpret this verse to mean that not even they will expect an answer from their former objects of worship

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r3.claim: One completion of the conditional is that they would have been saved from the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r3.anchor: whose completion would be, “they would have been saved from the Fire” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r4.claim: Another proposed completion is that they would have known the truth.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r4.anchor: they would have known the truth

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r5.claim: Some read the whole sentence as a complete conditional: they would have seen the punishment if they had been rightly guided.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r5.anchor: Some read the whole sentence as the complete conditional statement

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r6.claim: On that reading, they may be the idolaters, who if guided in this world would have known to fear the punishment in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r6.anchor: they may refer to the idolaters, who, had they been rightly guided in the world, would have had known to fear the punishment in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:28:64/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r7.claim: Alternatively, they may be the idols, which would see the punishment if they were living beings capable of being guided.
STUDYQURAN:28:64/r7.anchor: or they may refer to the idols, which would see the punishment if they were actually living beings capable of being guided (R)

TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r1.claim: The idolaters are told to call the partners they worship besides God, as in 7:195.

TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r2.claim: They call those partners, but the partners do not answer them, as the wording is also explained in 18:52.

TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r3.claim: They see the punishment with their own eyes; al-Ṭabarī links the expression to 2:166.

TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r4.claim: When they see the punishment, they wish they had followed the truth in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v18p296#2/r4.anchor: فودوا حين رأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا في الدنيا مهتدين للحق

TABATABAI:28:63-66/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r5.claim: The idolaters call on supposed partners to save them and repel the punishment; the following mention of seeing the punishment clarifies the failed appeal.
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r5.anchor: والمراد بدعوتهم دعوتهم إياهم لينصروهم ويدفعوا عنهم العذاب ولذا قال { ورأوا العذاب } بعد قوله

TABATABAI:28:63-66/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r6.claim: One reading supplies an omitted result: if they had been guided, they would have seen the punishment, meaning they would have recognized it as true.
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r6.anchor: قيل جواب لو محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه والتقدير لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون لرأوا العذاب أي اعتقدوا أن العذاب حق

TABATABAI:28:63-66/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r7.claim: Another possible reading takes “if only they had been guided” as a wish that they had been guided.
TABATABAI:28:63-66/r7.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون لو للتمني أي ليتهم كانوا يهتدون

TABRISI:28:63-64/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:63-64/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:63-64/r3.claim: The followers are told to summon the beings they worshipped to rescue them from God’s punishment; they are called partners only because the followers falsely claimed partnership by worship.
TABRISI:28:63-64/r3.anchor: وإنما أضاف الشركاء إليهم لأنه لا يجوز أن يكون لله شريك

TABRISI:28:63-64/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:63-64/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:63-64/r4.claim: They call the alleged partners, who do not grant their plea, and they see the punishment.
TABRISI:28:63-64/r4.anchor: أي فيدعونهم فلا يجيبونهم إلى ملتمسهم

TABRISI:28:63-64/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:63-64/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:63-64/r5.claim: The conditional’s answer is omitted; the author prefers ‘if they had been guided, they would have recognized the punishment as true,’ since the context signals the ellipsis.
TABRISI:28:63-64/r5.anchor: جواب لو محذوف تقديره لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون لرأوا العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r1.claim: The command is addressed to the unbelievers among the children of Adam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وقيل} أي: لكفار بني آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r2.claim: They are told to call on their idols for help and rescue from the punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r2.anchor: أي: استعينوا بآلهتكم التي كنتم تعبدونها. أي: لينصروكم ويخلصوكم من العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r3.claim: The idols did not answer them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi compares this scene with the command to call on the partners in Surat al-Kahf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r4.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية في: الكهف [52]؛ قوله: {ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r5.speaker: المفسرون وأهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r5.claim: They say the conditional sentence has an omitted answer: had they been guided in this world, they would not see punishment in the next or have followed the idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p435/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون وأهل المعاني: جواب {لو} محذوف، على تقدير: لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا ما رأوا العذاب في الآخرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r1.claim: The disbelievers are told to call upon the beings they worshipped besides God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r1.anchor: من كنتم تعبدون من دون الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r2.claim: The idols give them no reply that can benefit them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:64-66/r3.claim: Had they been guided, they would not have followed the idols and would not have seen the punishment.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r3.claim: The partners they are told to call are the idols.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r3.anchor: قال:} وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم { [القصص: 64] ، يعني: الأوثان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r4.claim: The idols do not respond, and the worshippers enter the punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r4.anchor: } فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب { [القصص: 64] ، أي: ودخلوا العذاب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r5.claim: If they had been guided in worldly life, they would not have entered the punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r5.anchor: } لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون { [القصص: 64] ، أي: لو أنهم كانوا مهتدين في الدنيا ما دخلوا العذاب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r6.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r6.claim: Another view says that if they had followed worldly guidance as they recognized it in the afterlife, they would not enter punishment; their afterlife belief is not accepted.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p604/r6.anchor: وبعضهم يقول: لو كانوا مهتدين في الدنيا كما أبصروا الهدى في الآخرة ما دخلوا العذاب، وإيمانهم في الآخرة لا يقبل منهم.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r1.claim: The polytheists are mockingly told to summon the beings they worship to save them from punishment; the supposed gods cannot help or even answer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r1.anchor: Onlar da tanrılarından yardım isterler, ancak tanrıları yardım etmek şöyle dursun onlara cevap dahi veremezler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r2.claim: The regretful wish is voiced on behalf of unbelievers, who will lament not choosing the right path in worldly life after seeing the punishment for associating partners with God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:64/r2.anchor: onların Allah’a ortak koşmanın cezasının ne olduğunu görünce dünyada iken doğru yolu seçmediklerine hayıflanacaklarını dile getirmektedir

BURHAN:v3p185/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p185/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p185/r5.claim: The omitted result may be that, had they been guided in worldly life, they would not see punishment in the next, or would not have followed the false partners.
BURHAN:v3p185/r5.anchor: أي يهتدون في الدنيا لما رأوا العذاب في الآخرة أو لما اتبعوهم

SAMIN-DURR:28:64/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:64/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:64/r1.claim: The response to law is omitted: either “when they saw the punishment” or “to repel it.”
SAMIN-DURR:28:64/r1.anchor: جوابها محذوف أي: لما رأوا العذاب أو لدفعوه

ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r1.claim: The partners did not answer them with an argument.

ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r2.claim: The response to لو is omitted: had they been guided, they would not have followed the partners or seen punishment.
ZAJJAJ:v4p151/r2.anchor: المعنى لو كانوا يهتدون لما اتبعوهم ولا رأوا العذاب

ASAD-NOTES:28:64#n68/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:64#n68/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:64#n68/r1.claim: The phrase refers to the beings or powers whom the audience treated as God's partners.
ASAD-NOTES:28:64#n68/r1.anchor: Lit., "those (God-)partners of yours": see note 64 above.

QIRAAT-ER:28:64:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:64:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:64:2#1/r1.claim: Ishmām blends a trace of the active ḍamma with the passive kasra on qāf, signaling the underlying active form while retaining passive morphology.
QIRAAT-ER:28:64:2#1/r1.anchor: the qāf receives a combined ḍamma-kasra (ishmām), blending the passive-voice kasra with a trace

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r1.claim: The call to invoke their partners is public rebuke and mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r1.anchor: تقريعا لهم وتهكما بهم ( ادعوا شركاءكم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r2.claim: One view says there is no genuine request and the people call in bewilderment; another says they obey a real command meant to expose helpless idols publicly.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : دعوهم لضرورة الامتثال على أن هناك طلبا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r3.claim: The fa after the imperative appears to signal a genuine command, though the alternative more forcefully emphasizes humiliation.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر من تعقيب صيغة الأمر بالفاء في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r4.claim: The partners cannot answer or help their worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r4.anchor: ضرورة عدم قدرتهم على الاستجابة والنصرة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r5.claim: Another possibility is that the partners are occupied or their mouths have been sealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد فلم يجيبوهم لأنهم في شغل شاغل عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r6.claim: The pronoun apparently refers to callers; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says both callers and called saw the punishment, while an unendorsed view refers only to the called.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r6.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير للداعين وقال الضحاك : هو للداعين والمدعوين جميعا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r7.claim: Seeing may mean seeing punishment's beginnings, seeing it as if present, or cognitively recognizing it; the last reading omits a second object.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن الرؤية العذاب إما على معنى رؤية مباديه أو على معنى رؤيته نفسه بتنزيله منزلة المشاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r8.claim: Some grammarians disallow omission of the second object of cognition verbs; others parse 'connected to them' as a circumstantial phrase modifying punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r8.anchor: وتقدم آنفا عن البعض أن الأكثرين على المنع فمن منع وقال في بيان المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r9.claim: If لو is conditional, its omitted answer means either they would use a stratagem to avert punishment or the rightly guided would not see it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r9.anchor: لو شرطية وجوابها محذوف أي لو كانوا يهتدون لوجه من وجوه الحيل يدفعون به العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the objection that an affirmative seeing cannot signal a negated omitted result; the ellipsis follows sense and context.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r10.anchor: بأن الدال على المحذوف رأوا العذاب وهو مثبت فلا يقدر المحذوف منفيا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r11.claim: Alternatively, لو is optative, expressing their wish that they had been guided, so no conditional answer is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r11.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ( لو ) للتمني أي تمنوا لو أنهم كانوا مهتدين فلا تحتاج إلى الجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r12.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r12.claim: The optative is questioned because one expects 'if only we had been'; replies allow reported speech, bewildered longing, or God's compassionate speech by metaphor as in 2:103; al-Ṭībī calls it effect for cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p101#2/r12.anchor: وقال صاحب التقريب : فيه نظر إذ حقه أن يقال لو كنا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r1.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī insists لو is conditional but rejects omitted-answer analyses and offers three explicit readings to avoid breaking syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r1.anchor: واختار الامام الرازي أنها شرطية إلا أنه لم يرتض ما قالوه في تقدير الجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r2.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r2.claim: First reading: terror and dizziness leave people unable to see, so they do not see punishment because they see nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r2.anchor: أحدها أن الله تعالى إذا خاطبهم بقوله سبحانه : ( ادعوا شركاءكم ) فهناك يشتد الخوف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r3.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r3.claim: Second reading refers to idols, which would see punishment if alive and rightly guided; the rational plural follows the worshippers' belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r3.anchor: وثانيها أنه تعالى لما ذكر عن الشركاء وهي الاصنام إنهم لا يجيبون الذين دعوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r4.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r4.claim: Third reading takes seeing as inward knowledge: the unbelievers knew the punishment was real, if only they were guided.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r4.anchor: وثالثها أن يكون المراد من الرؤية رؤية القلب أي والكفار علموا حقية هذا العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī dismisses al-Rāzī's proposals as unconvincing and more obscure than ordinary omitted-answer readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p102/r5.anchor: ولعمري أنه لم يأت بشيء وما يرد عليه أظهر من أن يخفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r1.claim: The disbelievers are told to call their idols to save them from punishment, but the idols do not answer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r1.anchor: {وقيل} للكفار: {ادعوا شركاءكم} أي: الأصنام لتخلصكم من العذاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r2.claim: The apodosis of law is omitted: had they been guided in worldly life, they would not have seen the punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p217#2/r2.anchor: على تقدير: لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا ما رأوا العذاب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r1.claim: They call on their partners out of extreme bewilderment, but the partners cannot answer or help; the punishment is clinging to them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r2.claim: They might wish they had found some stratagem to repel the punishment or had been guided to truth when they saw it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r2.anchor: لوجه من الحيل يدفعون به العذاب، أو إلى الحق لما رأوا العذاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:64-66/r3.claim: لو expresses a wish here: they wished they had been guided.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r1.claim: The second command to call the partners is delivered mockingly, to humiliate followers who answer anyone’s order.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r1.anchor: اي ثانيا للأتباع تهكما للاستهانة بهم , وأنهم من الذل والصغار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r2.claim: The partners are called theirs because their claim arose only from giving the idols their own wealth, speech, time, and conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r2.anchor: لم يستفيدوا زعمهم أنهم شركاء الله تعالى الله عن ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r3.claim: They call in desperate confusion, clinging to what cannot help, but the partners do not answer because they cannot perceive or act and are themselves doomed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r3.anchor: تعللا بما لا يغني , وتمسكا بما يتحقق أنه لا يجدي , لفرط الغلبة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r4.claim: Everyone sees the punishment and knows it will reach them with no one able to prevent it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r4.anchor: عالمين بأنه مواقعهم لا مانع له عنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r5.claim: The phrase can express regret that they had no guidance, or mean that guidance in their nature would have saved them, spared them seeing punishment, or kept them from following idols.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r5.anchor: أي يحصل منهم هدى ساعة من الدهر , تأسفا على أمرهم , وتمنيا لخلاصهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r6.claim: The passage turns from the impossibility of rescue without guidance to the coming inquiry about the messengers, after the question about God’s due.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p510/r6.anchor: لا خلاص من ذلك الردى إلا بالهدى , أتبعه الإعلام بأنه لا يمكن أحدا هناك

DURR-FULL:v6p432/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p432/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p432/r4.claim: The children of Adam are told to call their partners; the partners do not answer or do them any good.
DURR-FULL:v6p432/r4.anchor: وقيل لبني آدم {ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم} ولم يردوا عليهم خيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses their failure to respond as giving them no good answer or reply.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم بخير ولم يردوا عليهم خيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses يهتدون as يعرفون, meaning that they know or recognize.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3000#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : يهتدون يقول : يعرفون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r2.claim: The address is to those summoned in 28:62; after they realize the rebuke concerns their idols and their leaders begin excusing them, the rebuke continues.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r2.anchor: فإن ذلك النداء كان توبيخا لهم على اتخاذهم آلهة شركاء لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r3.claim: The speaker is left passive because context makes God clear as the one who spoke.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r4.claim: The command offers them false hope, which is immediately followed by despair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r4.anchor: والأمر مستعمل في الإطماع لتعقب الإطماع باليأس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r5.claim: The partners are attributed to the addressees because they claimed those beings shared divinity with God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r6.claim: Their call is an appeal for help based on their worldly belief that the idols intercede; the idols’ failure to answer delivers the intended despair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r6.anchor: والدعاء دعاء الاستغاثة حسب زعمهم أنهم شفعاؤهم عند الله في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r7.claim: First reported reading: the phrase coordinates with the idols’ failure; they visually see afterlife punishment shown to them and know their partners cannot help, while the following clause begins independently.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r8.claim: Second reading: the conjunction is circumstantial; they have seen the afterlife punishment and are bewildered about escape when told to call their partners, while the next clause is independent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r8.anchor: أن تكون الواو للحال والرؤية أيضا بصرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r9.claim: Third reading: seeing means knowing, with the second object omitted; they know punishment has overtaken them, and the conjunction may coordinate or mark circumstance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r9.anchor: أن تكون الرؤية علمية ، وحذف المفعول الثاني اختصارا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r10.claim: Fourth reading takes لو as a wish expressing regret for their failure to follow guidance in worldly life, which alone could have kept them from punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r11.claim: The author’s fifth reading takes punishment as worldly: they saw traces of earlier denied nations’ punishment; if they had learned from it and believed the Prophet, they would have abandoned shirk and escaped greater punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p159/r12.claim: These several readings all contribute intended meanings, making the verse a concise expression with many meanings.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r1.claim: For the first three readings, لو is conditional with an omitted answer supplied by an omitted object of be guided: they would have found escape; كانوا reinforces the proposition, and the imperfect signals guidance now cut off.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r1.anchor: حرف شرط وجوابها محذوفا دل عليه حذف مفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r2.claim: In the fourth reading, كانوا retains its ordinary past sense, while the imperfect evokes the continuing guidance they regret losing, which must last until life’s end to benefit them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r2.anchor: حينئذ في موقعه الدال على الاتصاف بالخبر في الماضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r3.claim: The author’s worldly-punishment reading echoes the reminder that people lived in the dwellings of wrongdoers and saw what God did to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p161/r3.anchor: وهذا في معنى قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r7.claim: The partners are idols claimed as partners of God; the possessive reflects the unbelievers’ designation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r7.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أنه يقال للكفرة العابدين للأصنام الذين اعتقدوهم آلهة ادعوا شركاءكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r8.claim: Inert idols cannot answer; the unbelievers then see the punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r8.anchor: ثم أخبر أنهم دعوهم فلم يكن في الجمادات ما يجيب ورأى الكفار العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج وغيره من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others say the conditional answer is omitted: they would not have been punished, or would not have worshipped idols; the first expresses grace, the second regret.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r9.anchor: ذهب الزجاج وغيره من المفسرين إلى أن جواب لو محذوف تقديره لما نالهم العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r10.claim: Another group connects the conditional to what precedes: they wished they had been guided.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p294#2/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة لو متعلقة بما قبلها تقديره فودوا لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r1.claim: Disbelievers are told to call on their gods to rescue them from punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r1.anchor: وقيل لكفار بني آدم ادعوا شركاءكم أي استغيثوا بآلهتكم لتخلصكم من العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r2.claim: The alleged partners do not answer or help them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r2.anchor: فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم أي فلم يجيبوهم إلى نصرهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the answer to لو is omitted: if they had been guided, they would not have followed the gods or seen the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p236/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج جواب لو محذوف والمعنى لو انهم كانوا يهتدون لما اتبعوهم ولما رأوا العذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249#2/r4.claim: They are told to call their partners to rescue them as they had hoped in worldly life; the partners do not answer, and the people realize they are bound for Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p249#2/r4.anchor: ليخلصوكم مما أنتم فيه، كما كنتم ترجون منهم في الدار الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p250/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p250/r1.claim: Seeing the punishment, they wish they had been among the guided in worldly life; this resembles the failed call to idols and sight of Hell in 18:52–53.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p250/r1.anchor: أي: فودوا حين عاينوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا من المهتدين في الدار الدنيا.

MUQATIL:28:62-65/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r4.claim: The unbelievers are told to ask their idols whether they are gods; the idols do not answer, as in 18:52.
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r4.anchor: سألوهم فلم تجبهم الآلهة، نظيرها في الكهف

MUQATIL:28:62-65/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r5.claim: They see the punishment; had they been guided from error in worldly life, they would not see punishment in the hereafter.
MUQATIL:28:62-65/r5.anchor: يقول: لوأنهم كانوا مهتدين في الدنيا ما رأوا العذاب في الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r1.claim: The partners they are told to invoke are the idols, called upon to rescue them from punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r2.claim: The idols did not answer those who called on them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p243#3/r3.claim: The answer to law is omitted; the implied completion is that they would not have seen the punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r6.claim: The idolaters are told to seek aid from the gods they worshipped in worldly life, asking them to rescue them from punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r6.anchor: أي استغيثوا بآلهتكم التي عبدتموها في الدنيا لتنصركم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r7.claim: They call upon the gods for aid.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r8.claim: The gods neither answer nor benefit their worshippers.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r8.anchor: أي فلم يجيبوهم ولم ينتفعوا بهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the jawab of law is omitted: guidance would have saved them and kept them from punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج: جواب { لو } محذوف والمعنى: لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r10.claim: One explanation is that, had they been guided, they would not have called upon the idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r10.anchor: وقيل: أي لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون ما دعوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r11.claim: Another explanation is that, on seeing punishment, they wish they had followed guidance in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:62-66/r11.anchor: وقيل المعنى: ودوا حين رأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا
